question.problem: The function $f(x)=4\operatorname{ln}⁡(kx-3)+1$ has an inverse function given by ${f}^{-1}(x)=\frac{1}{3}\cdot {e}^{(x-1)/4}+1.$ What is the value of $k?$

current_example.worked_solution:
To find $f^{-1}(x),$ we start by replacing $f(x)$ with $y\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =2{log}_{4}⁡(3x)-1\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we swap $x$ and $y{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =2{log}_{4}⁡(3y)-1\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we make $y$ the subject of the equation, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =2{log}_{4}⁡(3y)-1 \\ 2{log}_{4}⁡(3y) & =x+1 \\ {log}_{4}⁡(3y) & =\frac{x+1}{2} \\ {4}^{{log}_{4}⁡(3y)} & ={4}^{(x+1)/2} \\ 3y & ={4}^{(x+1)/2} \\ y & =\frac{1}{3}{4}^{(x+1)/2}\end{aligned}
$$

    

Therefore, the inverse function is $f^{-1}(x) =\dfrac13 4^{(x+1)/2}.$
